summary: Migrate locked manifests and authorize bounded autonomy

delivery.outcome: Migrate a hash-locked legacy target manifest safely and let an explicit execution or autonomous user request authorize bounded implementation without a redundant confirmation prompt
nonGoals: No downstream repository mutation in this ticket
No new dependency, schema version or target-owned field
No destructive or out-of-scope authority, secret handling, force push or agent self-approval
No VERSION, tag, GitHub Release or immutable standard publication

architecture.decision: Use the exact legacy target manifest authenticated by its installed lock hash as the previous structural merge base; treat an explicit execution or autonomous user request as bounded session authorization while preserving separate hard-safety and trusted-merge boundaries
interfaceChanges: Legacy managed target manifests can migrate into the extendable manifest contract
An explicit execution or autonomous request authorizes bounded implementation without a second confirmation
dataChanges: Successful legacy upgrade creates the managed .governance/manifest.base.json artifact
architecture.rollback: Revert ticket-046 before its separate immutable patch release; existing v0.14.0 remains unchanged

validation.evidence: Locked legacy content is accepted and hash mismatch fails closed
Legacy, fresh and extendable upgrades preserve their declared ownership boundaries
Goal-shaped regression and every maintained Linux suite pass
Published PR head passes both required checks and independent approval
Hub and managed agent contracts permit bounded autonomous execution while preserving hard safety and exact-head merge approval
